data.title: Piotr Wozniak
data.contentMarkdown:
# Piotr Wozniak

Creator of [[z2oUypiCEtPaDqNjbUsawCj:::Supermemo]] and popularizer of [[z2D1qPwddPktBjpNuwYFVva:::Spaced repetition memory system]] and [[zHwr5v9VJGX3MzHyzz4V8wt:::Incremental reading]].

contextBlocks: The first consumer system of this kind was [[z2oUypiCEtPaDqNjbUsawCj:::Supermemo]], created by [[zT8N3LTbePn2LVD7ZhJ5TLr:::Piotr Wozniak]]. It adopted and popularized the term “spaced repetition”; prior literature had used a variety of terms (often referring to more specific facets of the underlying phenomenon).

The original digital [[z2D1qPwddPktBjpNuwYFVva:::Spaced repetition memory system]], created by [[zT8N3LTbePn2LVD7ZhJ5TLr:::Piotr Wozniak]]. Includes support for various related personal information management systems, such as [[zHwr5v9VJGX3MzHyzz4V8wt:::Incremental reading]].

[[zT8N3LTbePn2LVD7ZhJ5TLr:::Piotr Wozniak]] uses retrievability and stability in his analysis; [[zYPeHVeq311Jh4whSstyeFX:::Robert A. Bjork]] and Bjork (1992) call an analogous pair of parameters retrieval strength and storage strength, respectively.

backlinkedNotes.linkingNoteTitle: Piotr Wozniak - Effective learning - Twenty rules of formulating knowledge
To what extent is it helpful to use a memory system to reinforce aspects of a concept you don’t really understand?
contextBlocks: [[zT8N3LTbePn2LVD7ZhJ5TLr:::Piotr Wozniak]] says “Understand before you memorize”, but I wonder… is it truly never valuable to start reinforcing *bits* of a concept before you can really see the whole? Can knowing the bits make it easier to see the whole?
